purpose: Improve language-model candidate discrimination and deployable vessel-ID contribution; proposal only.
hypothesis: Hard-negative ranking, better pair coverage and Korean transliteration diversity may improve fixed-candidate ranking; OOF fusion and constrained forward decoding may turn this into ID accuracy.
changed_factors: Separate proposed comparisons: within-language sampling without replacement; row-mean CE; hard-negative ranking; Korean augmentation; HCX catalog-constrained decoding; cross-fitted score fusion.
fixed_conditions: No new model training/inference or ZIP generation in this planning task.
Fit-fold-only dictionaries, mining, augmentation and tuning; official catalog only.
Keep retrieval, base matcher assets and candidate budgets fixed for the first reverse-model comparisons.

data.split_id: G5-s42; planned outer regression and fit-internal tuning

training_pairs.negative_rule: planned: competing distinct catalog names from fit-only retrieval; exclude all same-name IDs
training_pairs.positive_rule: fit-fold observed name -> official catalog name

model.loss: planned: retained SFT plus listwise rank loss; row-mean CE as a separate ablation
model.type: HyperCLOVA X 0.5B forward/reverse LoRA; existing ByT5 as a later controlled representation comparison

commands: PowerShell Get-Content/ConvertFrom-Json on existing experiment records and source; no Python execution.
observations: Existing V2 records: 6814 pairs, 2400 replacement draws, 1700 Korean/700 non-Korean.
Korean pairs increased from 305 to 367; non-Korean from 4380 to 6447.
No hard-negative training in current conditional LM CE.
HCX-05 evaluation subobject records Korean generated exact 23/64 and post-generation catalog-name search Top1 46/64, Top10 55/64.
ByT5 already implements a byte-token trie; HCX currently free-generates then performs approximate catalog search.
interpretations: Uneven coverage is an exposure diagnosis, not proof of underfitting.
Ranking objectives are the top proposed model change; existing results do not prove official-score improvement.
limitations: No new accuracy, timing or retrieval measurements.
Proposed hyperparameters are initial comparisons, not validated optima.
Same-name IDs cannot be resolved using a name-only likelihood.
Outer/inner cross-fitting is necessary for learned score fusion.
Historical severe scores use gold-selected errors and partial Break checks; use the audit interpretation.
decision: Plan recorded; prioritize deployable V1/V2 diagnosis then isolated coverage/loss/ranking changes. Preserve existing source, model assets and archives.
next_actions: Prepare the required server-compatible environment before execution.
Use a new run ID and predeclared paired comparison for each implemented change.
Evaluate name candidate inclusion, conditional LM rank, final ID Fix/Break, language metrics and cost separately.
